extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy analysts, and foundation staff studying foundation grantmaking and Hispanic/Latino support
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and evaluation criteria for identifying, classifying, and analyzing foundation grants benefiting Hispanics/Latinos in the U.S., including data-source use, coding rules, quality-control procedures, regional and field categorizations, and reporting metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice to insure credibility of foundation research studies
rubrics_metrics.description: When promoting research studies, the NCRP should advise researchers on necessary measures to insure credibility for each research study conducted on foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recommendation for an oversight/advisory role: researchers should be advised about methodological measures required to make studies credible. (Context: listed among suggestions for improving the state-of-the-art in foundation research.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Council on Foundations engagement and response-rate assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council on Foundations should engage in its own research and assist researchers in obtaining higher rates-of response from foundations included in survey studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: CF should both produce research and help improve primary data collection (e.g., boosting survey participation) to improve data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and correct Foundation Center codification/description system
rubrics_metrics.description: The system used by the Foundation Center staff for the codification and description of grants should be examined. Errors in the data banks must be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actionable item: audit coding schema and data-entry processes; identify and fix inaccuracies in the Foundation Center data banks (FGI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Foundation Grants Index (FGI) with caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers on foundation grant‑making activities should be encouraged to use the Foundation Grants Index data base whenever possible, instead of using only IRS forms 990-A which offer extremely limited information. Also, FGI should not be an exclusive source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: FGI is a richer data source than 990-A but should be supplemented with other sources; do not rely solely on any single source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage foundations to include informative annual-report grant descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should be encouraged to include in their Annual Reports an informative/description of the purposes of their grants and the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of donees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: richer public reporting by foundations improves secondary research and data verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation collaboration for listing-accuracy checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the system used by the Foundation Center to code and describe listed grants is improved, foundations should collaborate in the quest for accuracy by examining the bi-monthly listing of grants made by the Foundation Center and published in Foundation News by the Council on Foundations. Foundations can then inform the Center of errors found in the listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance: foundations should proactively review published listings and report corrections to the Center to improve the public index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary classification dimensions for analyzing support to Hispanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Support by foundations to Hispanics is examined under the following classifications: foundations acting as donors; groups designated as recipients; ethnicity of beneficiaries; Hispanic control of recipient boards of directors; geographic coverage of grants; fields of interest in which grants were awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These represent the analytic dimensions used to structure the study and should be captured for each grant record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria for grant selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants awarded to Hispanic or 'Spanish-speaking' organizations, or for the benefit of Hispanics living in the United States, excluding grants given to Puerto Ricans living in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, were extracted for further investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit inclusion: U.S.-based Hispanic beneficiaries or Spanish-speaking organizations. Explicit exclusion: Puerto Rico residency grants. Apply consistently during search and extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnicity categorization of beneficiary (Chicano, Puerto Rican, General Hispanic, Mixed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories used to classify grants according to ethnicity: (1) Chicano — grants given to Mexican American recipients and/or for benefit of Mexican American persons; (2) Puerto Ricans — grants given to Puerto Rican recipients in the United States and/or for the benefit of Puerto Ricans in the U.S.; (3) General Hispanic — grants given to Spanish and/or Hispanic recipients not clearly Chicano or Puerto Rican; (4) Mixed — grants given to benefit one or several Hispanic minorities and other non-Hispanic minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the study's working definition of 'Hispanic' as a variety of Spanish-origin groups (Chicano, Puerto Rican, Cuban, other Spanish-speaking Caribbean and Latin American residents in the U.S.), synonymous with 'Latino.' Use these category labels when coding ethnicity of beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific coding assumptions when classifying grants
rubrics_metrics.description: The following assumptions were made when classifying grants: (a) All grants given to an agency having 'La Raza' as part of its legal title were considered Chicano; (b) All grants given to agencies having a special reference to Puerto Rican history and culture as part of their legal names were considered Puerto Rican; (c) Institutions thus assumed as Chicano or Puerto Rican were also assumed to be minority controlled; (d) Grants to provide 'bilingual,' 'bicultural' (or both) services, in states and cities with a high concentration of Hispanic populations, or when Hispanics were the largest average ethnic minority, were assumed to be Spanish-English bilingual, and therefore related to the Hispanic population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit heuristics for uniform coding when grant descriptions are ambiguous; the study also performed random telephone confirmation of these assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual search and extraction methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The present study utilizes the Foundation Grants Index (for 1977 and 1978) on the basis of a manual search across 29,674 entries to identify and analyze grants which support Hispanics. Grants selected from the Index were recorded on note cards by a Hispanic recorder. One card was prepared for each grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual extraction steps: search FGI entries manually; create one record (note card) per grant; use human coders familiar with the population for initial extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data recording, cross-checks, and quality-control procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: With a second enumerator, the recorder checked the note cards against the Index for omissions, duplications, and errors. All grant cards were then photocopied in sets of different colors for a preliminary analysis (white - arranged by grantees; green - arranged by foundations; peach - arranged by ethnicity of recipients; yellow - arranged by fields of interest). The copies were again checked to assure that all card sets were equal. Inaccuracies discovered in the Index entries were corrected through telephone conversations or information provided by foundations. Spot checks were made to further reduce undetected inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple independent checks, color-coded parallel card sets sorted by different keys, and follow-up calls to foundations are prescribed quality-control measures. Photocopying and cross-sorting help detect omissions/duplications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of 'national' grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants intended to benefit all regions were classified as 'national.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional analyses should exclude national grants when calculating adjusted regional distributions, per the study's approach (see adjusted percentages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional grouping definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The eighteen states in which grants were awarded for the benefit of Hispanics were grouped into regions: Northeast (Connecticut, Massachusetts, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, District of Columbia); North Central (Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Wisconsin, Nebraska); Southwest (Colorado, Arizona, California, Texas, New Mexico).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these explicit region-to-state mappings when aggregating geographic distributions; the study also compares regional funding shares to U.S. Census Hispanic population percentages and presents an 'adjusted' regional distribution excluding national-purpose funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of interest categorization and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundation support for Hispanic needs and concerns can be separated into eight broad fields of interest: (a) Social Services — services to individuals, youth, families and migrants (including bilingual/bicultural services and general organizational support); (b) Community Organization and Development — efforts to improve social and economic conditions through coalitions and citizen action (distinct from social services); (c) Civil Rights and Legal Services — litigation, voter registration, legal services, publications, legal education/internships; (d) Research — research activities of direct relevance to Hispanics; (e) Education — educational leadership, scholarships, bilingual/bicultural education, adult and remedial education; (f) Health — physical and mental health services, training in health professions; (g) Arts and Humanities — library collections, music instruction, Hispanic performing arts, exhibits, films; (h) Religion — action of Hispanic churches, theological fellowships, conferences of Hispanic bishops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational definitions for coding field of interest for each grant; the report provides examples of large grants per field and reports relative shares (e.g., Education 30%, Civil Rights 25%, Research 12%, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic/reporting metrics to capture for each grant and aggregate
rubrics_metrics.description: Key metrics reported and compared include: number of grants; total dollar value; grants as percent of all grants; average grant amount; number of foundations supporting Hispanics; percent of dollars allocated to Hispanic-controlled vs non-Hispanic-controlled agencies; distribution of dollars by ethnicity of beneficiaries; frequency of individual foundation support (how many grants per foundation); regional distribution of funds; field-of-interest distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should compute both counts and dollar values, percent shares, averages, and cross-tabulations (e.g., ethnicity × agency control, region × field) and compare to prior studies for trend inference with caution about differing methods/years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling skew and outliers in category totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that single large grants can skew category percentages (e.g., a $2,950,487 ETS fellowship grant skews the 'Mixed' category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting category shares, identify and note individual large grants that disproportionately affect aggregate percentages; consider reporting medians or excluding extreme outliers in sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost and practicality considerations for computerized systems
rubrics_metrics.description: While a computerized system might have been equally helpful, the cost could well have proved prohibitive since searches had to be carried out constantly and FGI inaccuracies repeatedly checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the potential efficiency of computerized searches against expected costs and the need for repeated human verification where source data are error-prone; plan for ongoing verification if adopting computerized methods.
